title: Event-frame discipline (events-frames-taint-§1)
cluster_summary: Two of the three findings are real §1 breaches, and both are small. PFE keeps a private CreateFrame watcher even though it embeds AceEvent, which §1 line 36 forbids explicitly. WG has one bare self:RegisterEvent left outside the pcalled helper. Each fix is local to its repo. No upstream change is needed, because §1 already answers PFE's (event, target) collision: use a separate AceEvent target, as PFE's own Providers.lua does. PC-R-12 is refuted. PrettyChat embeds no AceEvent, so its named watcher falls under the carve-out, and no rule forbids naming a frame.

verdicts.assessment: Real breach. core/PartyFrameEnhanced.lua:122 creates a CreateFrame watcher in an addon that embeds AceEvent, and events-frames-taint.md:36 removes the carve-out explicitly in that case. The standard does not need amending, because a dedicated Embed({}) target already avoids the (event, target) collision and modules/Providers.lua already uses one. The finding is wrong on one point: the registration already goes through NS.SafeRegisterEvent (:128), and a disarm already exists. No player impact.
verdicts.remediation: Replace regenWatch with a dedicated AceEvent target that is not the addon object (LibStub('AceEvent-3.0'):Embed({})), as modules/Providers.lua does. Keep NS.SafeRegisterEvent. The handler unregisters PLAYER_REGEN_ENABLED and then calls flushSecure(). disarmPendingRegen unregisters it by name. Keep NS.PendingRegenArmed truthful by tracking an armed flag, or by checking the target's registration. Update the comment at :112-116 and the 'own frame' wording at docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:199 and :269. Write the characterization test first.

verdicts.assessment: core/WhatGroup.lua:436 is a bare self:RegisterEvent, which breaks the §1 MUST that every registration go through the pcalled helper. It also makes the ARCHITECTURE.md:184-186 claim false. The runtime risk is latent, because the same event is already registered through the helper at login. The fix is a one-line swap.
verdicts.remediation: Change it to NS.SafeRegisterEvent(self, "PLAYER_REGEN_ENABLED", "OnDisabledCombatEnded", NS.RejectedEvents). A __badEvents pin in tests/test_disabled.lua is optional.

verdicts.assessment: No standard rule forbids named frames. PrettyChat embeds no AceEvent, so its lazy combat watcher is within the §1 boundary-watcher carve-out. The prefixed global name is deliberate and helps with /etrace, and the reviewer's own verdict was no change.
